Issued at 222 PM CDT Wed Jul 22 2026

Rest of Today - Tonight:

Despite high pressure over the region today, partly cloudy to
mostly cloudy skies persist across much of the Northland this
afternoon into early evening, with the highest coverage in the
Arrowhead and northwest Wisconsin. High temperatures this
afternoon top out in the low to upper 70s along with dry
conditions. Winds become calm to light tonight with comfortable
low temperatures in the upper 40s in north-central Wisconsin to
50s elsewhere. Some hazy skies return starting tonight for
portions of the area as wildfire smoke from out west inches back
into the Northland.

Late this Week - Early Next Week: 

The upper-level pattern across the CONUS remains amplified late
this week into early next week as a mid/upper-level ridge axis
over the western CONUS broadens and general troughing occurs
over eastern Canada and the eastern CONUS. This pattern will
leave the Upper Midwest in general northwest flow aloft, through
which periodic shortwave troughs traversing the flow will 
produce shower and thunderstorm chances at times for portions of
the Northland. 

The first round of precipitation would be a 10-20% chance in 
far northern Minnesota near the International Border for 
isolated showers Thursday morning, but a slightly better chance 
(20-30%) for isolated showers/non-severe storms Thursday 
afternoon and evening. The area of rain potential has been
trending slightly farther north. Very limited rainfall amounts 
are expected with this first round, mostly 0.10" or less unless 
a thunderstorm moves through, in which case very localized 
amounts to 0.25" cannot be ruled out. 

The best rain chances (30-90%; highest for the Iron Range, 
Arrowhead, and areas north) would be with a second shortwave 
trough and attendant surface cold front late Friday afternoon 
into Saturday morning. Forecast rainfall amounts with these
scattered showers and thunderstorms are mostly 0.2-0.5" north of
the Iron Range, 0.1-0.2" for the Iron Range, and 0.1" or less 
south of the Iron Range. The probabilities for localized amounts
>0.5" are only 20-40% in far northern Minnesota. Strong to
severe storms (Level 1 out of 5) are possible along and near the
cold front in north-central Minnesota late Friday afternoon into
Friday night with instability (MUCAPE 1000-1500 J/kg) and deep 
shear profiles (35-50 kt) favoring elevated supercell structures.
as there may be some weak capping that hangs around. If storms
stay elevated, this would favor large hail (up to quarter to
ping pong ball size) as the primary severe threat, though a 
secondary threat of damaging wind gusts to 60 mph couldn't be 
ruled out if the storms can become surface based. 

Depending on how quickly the cold front moves southeast through
the Northland on Saturday, there is a lower chance (10-20%) 
that storms could redevelop Saturday afternoon along and ahead 
of the cold front in portions of northwest Wisconsin and be 
capable of strong to severe storms with large hail and damaging 
winds as the main threat. However, the forecast trend with this
cold front has been speeding up its exit to the east of
northwest Wisconsin Saturday afternoon, so the more likely
scenario is that storms do not occur at all there Saturday PM. 

There are additional, sporadic shower and thunderstorm chances
(10-40%) for Sunday into Monday, but confidence remains low 
regarding location and precipitation potential due to
uncertainty in how far south any shortwave troughs rounding the
top of the mid/upper-level ridge can get into the Northland and
model soundings showing a fairly stout capping inversion for
most of the Northland both days. Should the area become
uncapped, both Sunday and Monday could see conditional, low-
confidence strong to severe storm potential. Overall, the
synoptic pattern through at least early next week does not favor any
notable, widespread precipitation.

Hot conditions and potential Heat Advisories for portions of 
the Northland return by this weekend into early next week. High 
temperatures gradually warm from the low to mid 80s on Thursday 
to mid-80s to low 90s on Saturday through Monday, though onshore
flow/lake breeze on Sunday would likely keep the hottest 
conditions away from Lake Superior and the Arrowhead. These 
hotter conditions combined with fairly low relative humidity and
breezy conditions at times could lead to a return of elevated 
fire conditions for Friday into early next week. 

Beyond Early Next Week:

Warmer than normal temperatures are favored for the end of July
into very early August, as well. This is highlighted by the CPC
8-14 day temperature outlooks and ensemble guidance, mainly due
to persistence of the mid/upper-level ridge over the western to
central CONUS.
